Maya Chen: quick sync  we need a small playbook for assertion propagation across hosted->dedicated->private. authz drift is getting noisy.
Luis Ortega: agree. single envelope header sounds right. what fields are essential?
Maya Chen: tid, caller, aid, flags, exp and sig-meta. compact JSON base64. prefer one header: X-RW-Assertion.
Ivy Patel: TTLs short (30s-2m) to limit replay. prefer HMAC for fast verify in hot paths.
Tom Novak: private customers require local KMS, so adapter translation at the edge is necessary. must preserve semantics (no privilege elevation).
Luis Ortega: fallback options for runtimes: reject, call adapter translate, or accept platform-signed if tenant allows. default to reject.
Maya Chen: observability: surface aid and truncated hash in traces; adapters MUST emit audit event mapping orig_aid->new_aid on translation.
Ivy Patel: add e2e tests: hosted->dedicated->private translation should fail when adapter drops or escalates flags.
Tom Novak: implement contract doc + mapping table for allowed flag transforms. include audit schema and metrics.
ops-bot: Created TODO 9410 in hosting-handbook: "Assertion envelope interop playbook". Assigned to @Maya Chen and @Tom Novak.
Maya Chen: action items: I draft RFC with header grammar + rollout plan; Luis -> verifier lib + reference shims; Tom/Ivy -> adapter contract + tests. Target: staging canary in 3w.
Luis Ortega: will spike verifier API today.
Ivy Patel: will add tests to eval suite.
Maya Chen: thanks all. will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
